paras.text: Lesson 13 — Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah (verses 1 to 54)
paras.urdu: سبق ۱۳ — سُوْرَةُ حٰمٓ السَّجْدَةِ (آیات: ۱ تا ۵۴)
paras.pashto: ۱۳ لوست — سورة حم السجده (آیتونه ۱ تر ۵۴)

paras.text: Reason for the name and introduction
paras.urdu: وجہ تسمیہ اور تعارف
paras.pashto: د نوم وجه او پېژندنه

paras.text: This surah begins with the letters Ha Mim, and in verse 37 is the word "sajdah" (prostration). With this connection its name is Ha Mim al-Sajdah. Its second name is "Fussilat" too, because this word has come in its first verse; further, it is also called "Surat al-Masabih" and "Surat al-Aqwat". It is a Makki surah. It is the second surah among the seven "Hawamim". Its subject is "practical Tawhid". In this surah there is a statement of calling towards the Oneness of the Exalted Lord. Since the most important means of calling towards Allah Almighty is the Qur'an-e-Hakim, therefore very important verses on the greatness of the Qur'an-e-Hakim have been stated in this surah.
paras.urdu: اس سورت کا آغاز حٰمٓ کے حروف سے ہوتا ہے اور آیت: ۳۷ میں لفظ سجدہ ہے۔ اس مناسبت سے اس کا نام حٰمٓ السَّجْدَةُ ہے۔ اس کا دوسرا نام فُصِّلَتْ بھی ہے، کیوں کہ اس کی پہلی آیت میں یہ لفظ آیا ہے، نیز اسے سُوْرَةُ الْمَصَابِيْحِ اور سُوْرَةُ الْأَقْوَاتِ بھی کہا جاتا ہے۔ یہ مکی سورت ہے۔ یہ سات "حوامیم" میں سے دوسری سورت ہے۔ اس کا موضوع ہے "توحیدِ عملی"۔ اس سورت میں توحیدِ باری تعالیٰ کی طرف بلانے کا بیان ہے۔ چوں کہ اللہ تعالیٰ کی طرف بلانے کا اہم ترین ذریعہ قرآنِ حکیم ہے، اس لیے اس سورت میں عظمتِ قرآنِ حکیم پر بہت اہم آیات بیان فرمائی گئی ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د دې سورت پیل د «حم» په تورو کېږي او په ۳۷ آیت کې د «سجده» کلمه ده؛ په همدې مناسبت یې نوم «حم السجده» دی. دویم نوم یې «فصلت» هم دی، ځکه چې دا کلمه یې په لومړي آیت کې راغلې؛ همدارنګه ورته «سورة المصابیح» او «سورة الاقوات» هم ویل کېږي. دا مکي سورت دی او له اوو «حوامیمو» څخه دویم سورت دی. موضوع یې «عملي توحید» ده. په دې سورت کې د باري تعالی توحید ته د بلنې بیان دی. څرنګه چې الله تعالی ته د بلنې تر ټولو مهمه وسیله قرآن حکیم دی، نو په دې سورت کې د قرآن حکیم د عظمت په اړه ډېر مهم آیتونه بیان شوي.

paras.pashto: 11. د مؤمنانو د عزت او اکرام یادونه

paras.urdu: ۱۶۔ رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم کی دعوتِ حق کا بیان

paras.pashto: 18. د حضرت موسی علیه السلام د تکذیب بیان

paras.pashto: 20. د توحید دلیلونه او د انسان د ناشکرۍ یادونه

paras.text: 21. A statement of the crookedness of the deniers, and mention of the signs of Allah Almighty present in the human self and in the universe

Lesson 13 — Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah (verses 1 to 54)

Reason for the name and introduction

This surah begins with the letters Ha Mim, and in verse 37 is the word "sajdah" (prostration). With this connection its name is Ha Mim al-Sajdah. Its second name is "Fussilat" too, because this word has come in its first verse; further, it is also called "Surat al-Masabih" and "Surat al-Aqwat". It is a Makki surah. Since the most important means of calling towards Allah Almighty is the Qur'an-e-Hakim, therefore very important verses on the greatness of the Qur'an-e-Hakim have been stated in this surah.

Central theme

A statement of the three beliefs (Tawhid, Prophethood and the Hereafter)

Basic themes

1. The greatness of the Qur'an and a statement of its various attributes

2. Declaration of the humanity of the Prophet of Islam (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)

3. Mention of the call to truth of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and a statement of the obstinacy and end of the polytheists of Makkah

4. Mention of the everlasting reward of the believers

5. The objection of the disbelievers to Tawhid and its answer with cosmic proofs

6. Allah Almighty alone is the Creator and Administrator of the universe

7. Lessons from the story of the nations that rejected the call of the messengers, and mention of the Resurrection

8. The testimony of their own limbs against the polytheists, and mention of the domination of the devils over the disbelievers

9. Enmity towards the Holy Qur'an and its end

10. A statement of showing steadfastness after accepting Allah Almighty as Lord

11. Mention of the honour and dignity of the believers

12. The command of patience, steadfastness and tolerance, that is, repaying evil with good, and mention of the divine rewards in return for it

13. A statement of the etiquette of preaching the religion and the method of protection from the attacks of Satan

14. Mention of prostrating only before Allah Almighty

15. Mention of the great power of Allah Almighty and the vastness of His knowledge

16. A statement of the call to truth of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)

17. Mention of the Holy Qur'an being guidance and healing and of the proof of its truth, and a statement of the evil end of those who deny the divine verses

18. A statement of the denial of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him)

19. The evil end of the disbelievers and the warning of severe punishment for those who deny the Resurrection

20. Proofs of Tawhid and mention of man's ingratitude

21. A statement of the crookedness of the deniers, and mention of the signs of Allah Almighty present in the human self and in the universe

۱۴۔ صرف اللہ تعالیٰ کے لیے سربسجود ہونے کا ذکر

۱۵۔ اللہ تعالیٰ کی عظیم قدرت اور علم کی وسعت کا تذکرہ

۱۶۔ رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم کی دعوتِ حق کا بیان

۱۷۔ قرآنِ مجید کے ہدایت اور شفاء ہونے اور اس کی حقانیت کے ثبوت کا ذکر اور آیاتِ الٰہی کے منکرین کے انجامِ بد کا بیان

۱۸۔ حضرت موسیٰ علیہ السلام کی تکذیب کرنے کا بیان

۱۹۔ کافروں کا انجامِ بد اور منکرینِ قیامت کے لیے شدید عذاب کی وعید

۲۰۔ توحید کے دلائل اور انسان کی ناشکری کا ذکر

۲۱۔ منکرین کی کج روی کا بیان اور انسانی جان اور کائنات میں موجود اللہ تعالیٰ کی نشانیوں کا تذکرہ

Lesson 13 — Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah (verses 1 to 54)

Reason for the name and introduction

This surah begins with the letters Ha Mim, and in verse 37 is the word "sajdah" (prostration). With this connection its name is Ha Mim al-Sajdah. Its second name is "Fussilat" too, because this word has come in its first verse; further, it is also called "Surat al-Masabih" and "Surat al-Aqwat". It is a Makki surah. It is the second surah among the seven "Hawamim". Its subject is "practical Tawhid". In this surah there is a statement of calling towards the Oneness of the Exalted Lord. Since the most important means of calling towards Allah Almighty is the Qur'an-e-Hakim, therefore very important verses on the greatness of the Qur'an-e-Hakim have been stated in this surah.

Central theme

A statement of the three beliefs (Tawhid, Prophethood and the Hereafter)

Basic themes

1. The greatness of the Qur'an and a statement of its various attributes

2. Declaration of the humanity of the Prophet of Islam (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)

3. Mention of the call to truth of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and a statement of the obstinacy and end of the polytheists of Makkah

4. Mention of the everlasting reward of the believers

5. The objection of the disbelievers to Tawhid and its answer with cosmic proofs

6. Allah Almighty alone is the Creator and Administrator of the universe

7. Lessons from the story of the nations that rejected the call of the messengers, and mention of the Resurrection

8. The testimony of their own limbs against the polytheists, and mention of the domination of the devils over the disbelievers

9. Enmity towards the Holy Qur'an and its end

10. A statement of showing steadfastness after accepting Allah Almighty as Lord

11. Mention of the honour and dignity of the believers

12. The command of patience, steadfastness and tolerance, that is, repaying evil with good, and mention of the divine rewards in return for it

13. A statement of the etiquette of preaching the religion and the method of protection from the attacks of Satan

14. Mention of prostrating only before Allah Almighty

15. Mention of the great power of Allah Almighty and the vastness of His knowledge

16. A statement of the call to truth of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)

17. Mention of the Holy Qur'an being guidance and healing and of the proof of its truth, and a statement of the evil end of those who deny the divine verses

18. A statement of the denial of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him)

19. The evil end of the disbelievers and the warning of severe punishment for those who deny the Resurrection

20. Proofs of Tawhid and mention of man's ingratitude

21. A statement of the crookedness of the deniers, and mention of the signs of Allah Almighty present in the human self and in the universe
